target_customer: Data centers, industrial users and government sites buying long-term power, plus fuel and isotope buyers
problem: Reliable emission free power from nuclear was slow and costly to build; Oklo aims to deliver small fast fission plants and sell power under long-term agreements.
business_model: Own and operate reactors selling power under long-term agreements, plus fuel recycling and isotope sales

founders.name: Jacob DeWitte
founders.background_notes: Background not on the YC page.

founders.name: Caroline Cochran
education: University of Oklahoma, B.S. mechanical engineering and B.A. economics

technical_complexity.rationale: Reactor design, fuel supply and an NRC licensing path are research grade and regulatory heavy, far beyond a small software team.

defensibility.rationale: Licensing and site permits take years and are costly to copy, though several other advanced reactor developers pursue similar paths.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied the wedge; the company listed via SPAC in 2024.

market_need_then: In 2014 clean firm power was wanted by climate focused investors, and small reactors were a funded concept; sources at the time on Oklo specifically were not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, concise and forward-looking with short declarative headlines

branding.community_and_virality: Retail investor attention after 2024 listing and a stock gain reported in 2025; press on its Altman link.

brand_strength.rationale: Name carries a nuclear history link, since Oklo is also the Gabon site of natural reactors, and the company gained wide press and a high profile ticker, but no brand study was found.

outcome_analysis: Oklo raised from Sam Altman linked investors and DCVC, reported as the first venture led Series A for a nuclear hardware company in 2018, then went public by merging with AltC in May 2024 with about 306 million dollars gross proceeds, below the 500 million marketed. The NRC rejected its first application in 2022 for insufficient information, but it returned in 2025 and began construction in Idaho, with AI power demand lifting its shares.
notes: Seed and Series A amounts not found. Axios says Altman led a 2015 Series A, DCVC says it led the Series A in 2018, a conflict not resolved. SPAC announced 2023-07 at 850M pre-money and 500M target, closed 2024-05-10 with about 306M trust, a WSJ figure of about 1.4B post-merger is single source. Totals on aggregators of 800M to 1.44B are unreliable. Name origin is not stated by any source; Oklo is also a Gabon region with natural reactors but that is not a sourced origin. The competitor search returned only 2025 to 2026 material so the list is empty. Founder DeWitte background was not on the YC page. No Altman role stated at founding beyond investor and later chairman who stepped down in April 2025.
